title: clock double-gating
scope: every archived run: divide_3d executed once every FOUR frames (engine every=2 x private self._k every=2), so all per-call quantities meant 4x what they said
detail: min_cycle/max_cycle are counted in DIVISION-CALLS and max_div/max_div_frac are PER-CALL throttles. Correcting the clock multiplied their wall-clock meaning by 4; the recipe that produced aspect 7.5 produced 3.2.

title: rescaling the fraction alone is masked by the floor
scope: the D1 correction itself, before this was noticed
detail: cap_div = max(max_div, max_div_frac*nF). The absolute floor DOMINATES at realistic cell counts (nF=1431: max(120, 42) = 120), so rescaling max_div_frac alone had NO effect. Both had to move. A correction that looks applied but is masked is worse than no correction, because it is believed.

title: composition-dependent dt
scope: any comparison across compositions that differ in whether RD is present
detail: dt = 1.0 if (cones and not rd) else 0.02 -- adding/removing the RD operators, the campaign's single most important edit, ALSO rescaled chemical:mechanical time 50x.
correction: one global dt for the whole campaign

title: recording-stride mismatch
scope: any run long enough to trip a recording stride > 1
detail: positions and topology recorded on different strides; the analysis paired one frame's coordinates with another frame's connectivity and reported phantom inverted cells ('97% hollow') that no physical fix could touch.

title: silently inert operators
scope: any composition with an unmet precondition -- i.e. exactly the combinations a SEARCH generates and a hand-written preset never did
detail: an operator whose prerequisite is missing no-ops, the run still finishes and still scores, so the loop records 'this mechanism cannot produce tubes' when the mechanism never ran. Manufactures FALSE IMPOSSIBILITY claims.
correction: acted-ledger; a run with an inert scheduled operator is not evidence

title: archive stored only the final frame
scope: every temporal observable, retrospectively -- the archive could not be re-scored for anything time-dependent without re-simulating
detail: the decisive evidence in the tube record is temporal (a protrusion peaking then degrading; a pattern flooding once growth starts; synchronised division waves).
correction: persist the full trajectory + per-frame metric table

title: vcap is weakly rate-coupled (my own claim retracted)
scope: the clock re-anchoring: cell count recovered (2927 vs ~2700) but aspect did not (1.73 vs ~7.5), so a rate-coupled quantity is still uncorrected
detail: I claimed vcap was not rate-coupled because "the same cells divide, only sooner". True of one cell, false of the population: vcap divisions bypass the throttle, so checking 4x more often means daughters start growing sooner and the total division count differs. The correct rescaling is not yet established.
correction: UNKNOWN -- requires a vcap sweep under the fixed clock

title: I compared two different metrics and called it a discrepancy
scope: my own analysis of the clock re-anchoring, and the vcap retraction reasoned from it
detail: I named our r95/median metric "aspect" and compared 1.73 against the report's "aspect ~7.5" for round_40_mc8 -- which is tube_len/tube_diam. tube_analysis.py:89 calls r95/median . Two different quantities. The lesson the document already states -- a numerical invariant is not the geometric one you meant -- applied to the analysis rather than the simulation. Fix: our metric is renamed , and tube_analysis (the archive OWN bank) is now computed on every run so comparisons against archived numbers use the archive definitions.
correction: rename to protr; compute tube_len/tube_diam via tube_analysis.analyze()

title: the same naming collision, committed again one function later
scope: the reconciliation summary: protr_final (tube_analysis, 40 sampled frames, its own body-median) collided with protr_peak (ours, all 901 frames), giving final > peak
detail: Having just diagnosed M1 -- comparing two different quantities under one name -- I merged tube_analysis output into our summary unprefixed and reproduced it. An impossible ordering (final > peak) is what exposed it. Fix: namespace as ta_*, so provenance is visible in the summary itself rather than inferred.
